newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Aug industrial output rises 8.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Aug industrial output rises 8.2 pct.

text.p: South Korea's industrial output in August rose 8.2 percent year-on-year from a 13.2 percent rise a year earlier, provisional National Statistical Office (NSO) figures showed on Thursday.
Aug July Aug 95
Industrial output +8.2 +8.1 +13.2
Ex-factory shipment +5.8 +6.7 +13.9
Inventories +18.3 +18.3 +12.4
Factory operation rate 83.5 82.7 82.5
Wholesale/retale saels +6.3 +6.8 +8.1
Domestic machinery orders +19.5 -0.7 +18.4
Import permits of machinery +1.7 +47.8 +17.9
Domestic construction orders +68.9 -12.7 +16.3
Note : figures in percent, year-on-year change.

A National Statistical Office statement attributed the August output rise to increased production by domestic oil refiners following their facilities expansion and to improving exports of cars and chemical products.
The statement said output of heavy industrial goods in August rose 11.6 percent year-on-year against 19.0 percent a year ago.
The statement said production of light industrial products fell 3.6 percent from a 2.2 percent decline a year earlier.
Ex-factory shipments for exports in August increased 2.9 percent year-on-year against a 27.8 percent rise a year before.

Exports of semiconductors fell to $12.55 billion for the eight months of this year against $12.98 billion a year earlier. This was the first decline in the value of South Korean semiconductor exports.
Shipment of domestic consumption products rose 6.9 percent compared with a rise of 9.3 percent a year ago.
The August shipments to the local market rose 0.4 percent month-on-month from a 4.8 percent rise a month ago due to sluggish ex-factory shipments of sedans, motorcycles and petroleum.
The August inventory still remained at high level of 18.3 percent due to rising stockpile of semiconductors and metal products, and slowing car sales at home, the statement said.
"The improvement in August figures doesn't mean our economy is out of its downturn curve," a National Statistical Office official said. "But the overall figures show it is not at risk."
